questions.question:
A capacitor \(C\) is first charged fully with potential difference of \(V_0\) and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance \(L\). In \(t\) s \(25\%\) of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of \(t\) is: (in s)
1. \(\dfrac{\pi \sqrt{{LC}}}{3}\)
2. \(\dfrac{\pi \sqrt{{LC}}}{6}\)
3. \(\dfrac{\pi \sqrt{{LC}}}{2}\)
4. \(\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{{LC}}{2}}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}\) Step:Find the value of\(t\). When a charged capacitor is connected to an inductor, the system executes \(LC\) oscillations. The total energy oscillates between the capacitor (electric field) and the inductor (magnetic field). Initial energy in the capacitor is given by; \(U_0 = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2_0\) At time \(t\), energy in the inductor is given by; \(U_L = U_0 \sin^2(\omega t)\) where,\( \omega = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\) According to the question,\(25\%\) of initial energy is in the inductor i.e., \(\Rightarrow U_L= \dfrac{1}{4}U_0\) \(\Rightarrow U_0\sin^{2}\omega t= \dfrac{1}{4}U_0\) \(\Rightarrow \sin^{2}\omega t= \dfrac{1}{4}\) \(\Rightarrow \sin\omega t= \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\Rightarrow\omega t= \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) \(\Rightarrow t= \dfrac{\pi}{6\omega}\) \(\Rightarrow t= \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{LC}}{6}\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

From the question, we can have the value of alternating voltage; \(\Rightarrow V(t)=220 \sin (100 \pi t) \) Now, the current value is given by; \(\Rightarrow I(t)=\dfrac{V(t)}{R} \) Substitute the known values we get; \(\Rightarrow I(t)=\dfrac{220}{50} \sin (100 \pi t) \) \(\Rightarrow {I}={I}_{\mathrm{m}} \sin (\omega {t}) \) Now, the time is given by the formula; \(t=\dfrac{\theta}{\omega} \) The sine waveform is maximum at the angle \(\pi / 2. \) \(\Rightarrow t_1=\dfrac{\pi}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{100 \pi}=\dfrac{1}{200} ~\text{sec}\) For, \(I=\dfrac{I_ m}{2}\) \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{I_m}{2}=I_m \sin \left(100 \pi t_2\right)\) \( \Rightarrow \sin \dfrac{\pi}{6}=\sin \left(100 \pi t_2\right) \quad\left[\because \sin \dfrac{\pi}{6}=\sin 60^{\circ}=\dfrac{1}{2}\right] \) \(\Rightarrow t_2=\dfrac{1}{600} ~\text s \) Required time: \(t_{\text {req }}=\dfrac{1}{200}-\dfrac{1}{600} \) \(\Rightarrow t_{\text {req }}=\dfrac{2}{600}\text{ s}\) \(\Rightarrow t_{\text {req }}=\dfrac{1}{300} \text{ s} \) \(\Rightarrow t_{\text {req }}=3.3 \text{ ms} \) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.
